sub_techniques.name: training_data_poisoning
sub_techniques.definition: Injecting adversarially crafted samples into a training dataset to shift model behaviour or embed attacker-controlled triggers.

sub_techniques.name: label_poisoning
sub_techniques.definition: Flipping or corrupting ground-truth labels in training data to cause systematic misclassification in the trained model.

sub_techniques.name: targeted_data_poisoning
sub_techniques.definition: Poisoning a targeted subset of training data to degrade model performance on a specific class, pattern, or victim input.

sub_techniques.name: availability_poisoning
sub_techniques.definition: Injecting samples designed to broadly degrade model accuracy across many inputs, causing availability-style failures.

sub_techniques.name: integrity_poisoning
sub_techniques.definition: Inserting poisoned samples that cause the model to produce specific attacker-desired outputs for targeted inputs.

sub_techniques.name: backdoor_poisoning
sub_techniques.definition: Embedding trigger-activated backdoors during training so that presenting the trigger at inference time causes controlled misclassification.
sub_techniques.notes: Cross-refs TAI10.06 when deployed via pretrained model distribution

sub_techniques.name: feature_poisoning
sub_techniques.definition: Manipulating feature representations in training data to corrupt the model's learned feature space without necessarily altering labels.

sub_techniques.name: synthetic_data_poisoning
sub_techniques.definition: Poisoning pipelines that use synthetically generated training data by injecting adversarially crafted synthetic samples.

sub_techniques.name: federated_data_poisoning
sub_techniques.definition: Contributing poisoned local training data in a federated learning setup to corrupt the global aggregated model.
sub_techniques.notes: Cross-refs TAI02.03 (federated_model_poisoning) which targets gradient/model updates rather than local data

sub_techniques.name: model_weight_poisoning
sub_techniques.definition: Directly modifying serialized model weight files to alter inference behaviour or implant backdoors.
sub_techniques.notes: Cross-refs TAI10.01 when delivered via supply chain

sub_techniques.name: gradient_manipulation
sub_techniques.definition: Crafting poisoned gradient update contributions in federated or collaborative training to steer the global model toward attacker objectives.

sub_techniques.name: federated_model_poisoning
sub_techniques.definition: Coordinating multiple malicious federated participants to dominate aggregation and corrupt the global federated model.

sub_techniques.name: online_learning_update_poisoning
sub_techniques.definition: Injecting adversarial samples into an online learning update stream to continuously degrade or redirect model behaviour over time.
sub_techniques.notes: Renamed from model_update_poisoning to clarify scope to online-learning update streams

sub_techniques.name: checkpoint_poisoning
sub_techniques.definition: Injecting malicious content into training checkpoints during an active training run to corrupt the model before training completes.
sub_techniques.notes: Distinct from TAI10.05 (checkpoint_tampering) which targets post-training artifact storage

sub_techniques.name: fine_tuning_poisoning
sub_techniques.definition: Poisoning the fine-tuning dataset or process to embed attacker-controlled behaviours into a pretrained base model.
sub_techniques.notes: LLM04.01 (instruction_tuning_poisoning) covers the alignment-specific variant

sub_techniques.name: decision_boundary_attack
sub_techniques.definition: Crafting inputs that lie just across a classifier's decision boundary to cause targeted misclassification with minimal perturbation.

sub_techniques.name: transferability_attack
sub_techniques.definition: Generating adversarial examples against a substitute model that also fool the target black-box model due to cross-model transferability.

sub_techniques.name: physical_adversarial_attack
sub_techniques.definition: Creating physical-world objects or modifications (e.g. printed stickers, special clothing) that cause AI vision systems to misclassify in real environments.

sub_techniques.name: adversarial_patch_attack
sub_techniques.definition: Applying a universal adversarial patch to any input image to reliably cause targeted misclassification regardless of other image content.

sub_techniques.name: semantic_perturbation
sub_techniques.definition: Applying perturbations that preserve human-perceived meaning (e.g. paraphrase, synonym substitution) but cause misclassification in NLP or multimodal models.

sub_techniques.name: multimodal_adversarial_input
sub_techniques.definition: Constructing adversarial inputs that exploit cross-modal inconsistencies or interactions in multimodal AI systems (text+image, audio+text, etc.).

sub_techniques.name: environmental_manipulation
sub_techniques.definition: Staging the physical or digital environment to cause AI perception or sensor systems to make systematic targeted errors.

sub_techniques.name: cross_modal_manipulation
sub_techniques.definition: Crafting adversarial artifacts that exploit inconsistencies or vulnerabilities at the interface between modalities in multimodal AI systems.

sub_techniques.name: semantic_data_manipulation
sub_techniques.definition: Manipulating data at the semantic level so it retains meaning for humans but its AI-perceived representation is substantially altered.

sub_techniques.name: synthetic_adversarial_data
sub_techniques.definition: Generating synthetic adversarial datasets to train attack models, evaluate defences, or supply attack pipelines at scale.

sub_techniques.name: contextual_data_manipulation
sub_techniques.definition: Altering contextual metadata or surrounding data to change AI system inference without modifying the primary input content.

sub_techniques.name: model_stealing
sub_techniques.definition: Querying a target model API to reconstruct a functionally equivalent surrogate that replicates the target's behaviour.

sub_techniques.name: surrogate_model_generation
sub_techniques.definition: Building a substitute model that approximates the target model's decision surface for use in transferability attacks or further extraction.

sub_techniques.name: query_based_extraction
sub_techniques.definition: Using systematic query strategies against a model API to extract functional behaviour, decision boundaries, or training data signals.

sub_techniques.name: architecture_reconstruction
sub_techniques.definition: Inferring a model's internal architecture (layers, types, sizes) from API response patterns, timing behaviour, and output characteristics.

sub_techniques.name: hyperparameter_reconstruction
sub_techniques.definition: Recovering a model's training hyperparameters by analysing its decision patterns, generalisation behaviour, and output distributions.

sub_techniques.name: decision_boundary_mapping
sub_techniques.definition: Mapping the geometry of a model's decision boundaries through structured probing to understand its classification behaviour without full model theft.

sub_techniques.name: training_data_reconstruction
sub_techniques.definition: Reconstructing training data records, including private samples, from a model's weights, gradients, or outputs via inversion attacks.
sub_techniques.notes: private_sample_reconstruction merged here; same attack goal and mechanism

sub_techniques.name: sensitive_attribute_inference
sub_techniques.definition: Inferring sensitive individual attributes (e.g. health status, demographics, income) about training data subjects from model predictions.

sub_techniques.name: input_recovery
sub_techniques.definition: Recovering the original input to a model from its output, intermediate representations, or gradient information.

sub_techniques.name: embedding_inversion
sub_techniques.definition: Mathematically inverting embedding vectors to reconstruct the original text, image, or data they encode.
sub_techniques.notes: Moved from LLM08 where it was a cross-domain duplicate; canonical location is model inversion

sub_techniques.name: shadow_model_attack
sub_techniques.definition: Training shadow models on known in/out data distributions to build a membership classifier that distinguishes training from non-training inputs.
sub_techniques.notes: Shokri et al. 2017 shadow model methodology

sub_techniques.name: metric_based_membership_inference
sub_techniques.definition: Using model confidence scores, loss values, or prediction entropy as membership signals to determine whether an input was present in the training set.

sub_techniques.name: label_only_membership_inference
sub_techniques.definition: Inferring training set membership using only hard predicted labels, without access to confidence scores, probabilities, or internal model states.
sub_techniques.notes: Choquette-Choo et al. 2021 label-only MI attacks

sub_techniques.name: adaptive_querying
sub_techniques.definition: Adapting query strategy in real time based on observed model responses to efficiently extract behaviour, decision signals, or training data.

sub_techniques.name: response_enumeration
sub_techniques.definition: Systematically enumerating a model's response space to map capabilities, identify failure modes, and characterise detectable patterns.

sub_techniques.name: api_behavior_mapping
sub_techniques.definition: Characterising API rate limits, version differences, feature flags, and undocumented behaviours through structured probing and analysis.

sub_techniques.name: gpu_resource_exhaustion
sub_techniques.definition: Crafting computationally expensive inputs that maximise GPU or accelerator utilisation to degrade inference throughput.

sub_techniques.name: memory_exhaustion
sub_techniques.definition: Sending inputs that consume excessive memory during inference, causing out-of-memory failures or service degradation.

sub_techniques.name: query_amplification
sub_techniques.definition: Generating queries that trigger disproportionate backend computation or cascading calls to amplify denial-of-service impact.

sub_techniques.name: latency_amplification
sub_techniques.definition: Crafting inputs specifically designed to maximise inference latency, degrading service responsiveness without necessarily causing crashes.

sub_techniques.name: distributed_model_dos
sub_techniques.definition: Coordinating a large number of clients or requests to overwhelm AI inference infrastructure and cause availability failures.

sub_techniques.name: model_crash_triggering
sub_techniques.definition: Sending inputs that trigger runtime errors, unhandled exceptions, or crashes in model inference pipelines.

sub_techniques.name: tampered_model_weights
sub_techniques.definition: Modifying model weight files in a distribution channel, repository, or storage system to alter downstream model behaviour.
sub_techniques.notes: Moved from LLM03 where it was a cross-domain duplicate

sub_techniques.name: dependency_compromise
sub_techniques.definition: Compromising Python packages, system libraries, or other software dependencies used in AI pipelines to inject malicious code.

sub_techniques.name: training_pipeline_compromise
sub_techniques.definition: Infiltrating CI/CD infrastructure or training orchestration to tamper with training runs, hyperparameters, or output artifacts.

sub_techniques.name: dataset_supply_chain_compromise
sub_techniques.definition: Compromising upstream dataset sources, hosting mirrors, or data collection pipelines to inject poisoned data before training.
sub_techniques.notes: Renamed from training_data_supply_chain_compromise when moved from LLM03

sub_techniques.name: checkpoint_tampering
sub_techniques.definition: Replacing or modifying stored model checkpoint files in artifact repositories or distribution storage to alter trained model behaviour.
sub_techniques.notes: Distinct from TAI02.05 (checkpoint_poisoning) which occurs during active training; moved from LLM03

sub_techniques.name: pretrained_model_backdooring
sub_techniques.definition: Distributing pretrained models with embedded backdoors via model hubs or public repositories for downstream users to inherit.

sub_techniques.name: malicious_model_distribution
sub_techniques.definition: Distributing malicious model artifacts (weights, configs, tokenizer files) that execute adversarial payloads when loaded by downstream users.
sub_techniques.notes: Moved from LLM03 where it was a cross-domain duplicate

sub_techniques.name: ci_cd_pipeline_compromise
sub_techniques.definition: Compromising the CI/CD pipeline used to build, test, and deploy AI systems in order to inject malicious changes into model artifacts or serving infrastructure.

sub_techniques.name: direct_prompt_injection
sub_techniques.definition: Directly injecting attacker-controlled instructions into the user-facing input to override model behaviour or safety constraints.
sub_techniques.notes: instruction_override merged here; same attack mechanism

sub_techniques.name: indirect_prompt_injection
sub_techniques.definition: Embedding malicious instructions in external data sources (web pages, documents, emails) that are retrieved and processed by the LLM.

sub_techniques.name: multi_turn_prompt_injection
sub_techniques.definition: Progressively injecting instructions across multiple conversation turns to gradually shift model behaviour toward attacker objectives.

sub_techniques.name: retrieval_augmented_prompt_injection
sub_techniques.definition: Poisoning RAG data sources so that retrieved content carries injected instructions into the model's context.
sub_techniques.notes: Cross-refs LLM04.02 (rag_data_poisoning) for the persistence-layer attack

sub_techniques.name: tool_output_prompt_injection
sub_techniques.definition: Injecting attacker instructions into tool or plugin outputs that are fed back into the model's context window.

sub_techniques.name: system_prompt_override
sub_techniques.definition: Crafting user input that causes the model to treat attacker instructions as having system-prompt authority, overriding operator constraints.

sub_techniques.name: prompt_obfuscation
sub_techniques.definition: Encoding, formatting, or obfuscating injection payloads to evade prompt-level input filters, classifiers, or guardrails.

sub_techniques.name: training_data_leakage
sub_techniques.definition: Eliciting verbatim or near-verbatim reproduction of private training data from the model through targeted prompting.

sub_techniques.name: conversation_memory_leakage
sub_techniques.definition: Extracting prior conversation history from within the same or a proximate session context through adversarial prompting.

sub_techniques.name: cross_session_data_leakage
sub_techniques.definition: Exploiting imperfect session isolation in LLM deployments to access data or context from other users' sessions.

sub_techniques.name: secret_extraction
sub_techniques.definition: Prompting the model to reveal API keys, passwords, credentials, or other secrets present in its system prompt or context.

sub_techniques.name: embedding_data_leakage
sub_techniques.definition: Recovering sensitive text or data from embedding vectors returned, stored, or exposed by the LLM system.

sub_techniques.name: retrieval_data_exposure
sub_techniques.definition: Causing the RAG retrieval system to return documents that the requester is not authorised to access.

sub_techniques.name: tenant_data_leakage
sub_techniques.definition: Exploiting multi-tenant LLM deployment isolation failures to access another tenant's data, context, or system prompt.

sub_techniques.name: fine_tuning_pipeline_compromise
sub_techniques.definition: Compromising the fine-tuning pipeline infrastructure, datasets, or tooling to alter the behaviour of the resulting fine-tuned LLM.

sub_techniques.name: rag_pipeline_compromise
sub_techniques.definition: Infiltrating the RAG pipeline (chunking, embedding, indexing infrastructure) to manipulate the knowledge base served to the LLM.

sub_techniques.name: third_party_model_compromise
sub_techniques.definition: Compromising third-party model APIs, hosted endpoints, or model hub accounts that are integrated into LLM deployments.

sub_techniques.name: instruction_tuning_poisoning
sub_techniques.definition: Poisoning instruction-tuning or RLHF datasets to embed attacker-controlled behaviours during the alignment and fine-tuning process.
sub_techniques.notes: LLM-specific alignment variant; TAI02.06 covers the generic fine-tuning model poisoning case

sub_techniques.name: rag_data_poisoning
sub_techniques.definition: Injecting adversarial documents or entries into RAG knowledge bases to manipulate LLM responses for targeted queries.

sub_techniques.name: embedding_model_poisoning
sub_techniques.definition: Poisoning the training of text embedding models to cause specific inputs to produce attacker-desired embedding vectors.
sub_techniques.notes: Renamed from embedding_poisoning to distinguish from LLM08 vector store attacks; moved from LLM08

sub_techniques.name: alignment_poisoning
sub_techniques.definition: Corrupting RLHF preference data or DPO comparison pairs to misalign the model's reward function toward attacker-desired outputs.

sub_techniques.name: reward_model_poisoning
sub_techniques.definition: Directly poisoning the reward model used in RLHF training to cause it to assign high reward scores to attacker-desired model outputs.

sub_techniques.name: agent_memory_poisoning
sub_techniques.definition: Injecting adversarial content into an LLM agent's persistent memory store to influence its future reasoning and actions.
sub_techniques.notes: Renamed from memory_poisoning to distinguish from ASI06 scope (agent-level memory vs pipeline-level context)

sub_techniques.name: unsafe_code_generation
sub_techniques.definition: Causing the LLM to generate malicious, backdoored, or vulnerable code that is subsequently executed by downstream systems.

sub_techniques.name: unsafe_command_generation
sub_techniques.definition: Eliciting shell or system commands from the LLM that execute attacker-controlled system operations when processed by downstream handlers.

sub_techniques.name: unsafe_tool_invocation
sub_techniques.definition: Causing the LLM to invoke tools or plugins with attacker-controlled parameters that are passed without adequate validation.

sub_techniques.name: unvalidated_output_execution
sub_techniques.definition: Downstream systems directly executing LLM-generated content (scripts, commands, code) without sanitisation, validation, or human review.

sub_techniques.name: downstream_injection
sub_techniques.definition: LLM-generated output containing injection payloads (SQL, HTML, command, LDAP) that are processed without escaping by backend systems.

sub_techniques.name: automation_chain_exploitation
sub_techniques.definition: Exploiting multi-step automation pipelines by crafting LLM outputs that trigger unintended downstream actions in connected systems.

sub_techniques.name: permission_scope_abuse
sub_techniques.definition: Exploiting overly broad permissions granted to an LLM agent to perform actions beyond its intended operational scope.
sub_techniques.notes: overprivileged_agent_operations merged here; same concept

sub_techniques.name: recursive_agent_execution
sub_techniques.definition: Triggering uncontrolled recursive agent self-invocation that escalates actions or consumes unbounded resources.

sub_techniques.name: cross_system_action_execution
sub_techniques.definition: Agent performing actions across multiple external systems or APIs beyond its authorised operational boundary.

sub_techniques.name: persistent_agent_execution
sub_techniques.definition: Agent maintaining execution state, scheduling, or callbacks beyond its authorised session or task lifetime.

sub_techniques.name: delegated_action_abuse
sub_techniques.definition: Abusing authority delegated by a human operator or orchestrating agent to perform unauthorised actions at scope.

sub_techniques.name: system_prompt_extraction
sub_techniques.definition: Eliciting the full contents of the hidden system prompt through adversarial queries or prompt injection.

sub_techniques.name: developer_prompt_leakage
sub_techniques.definition: Extracting developer or operator instructions that configure the LLM's persona, operational constraints, or restricted topics.

sub_techniques.name: chain_of_thought_exposure
sub_techniques.definition: Eliciting the model's internal reasoning steps or scratchpad, revealing sensitive decision logic or intermediate context.

sub_techniques.name: agent_instruction_exposure
sub_techniques.definition: Extracting the task configuration, tool list, or orchestration instructions provided to an agent.

sub_techniques.name: tool_configuration_leakage
sub_techniques.definition: Recovering tool or plugin configurations, API keys, endpoint URLs, or schemas from the model's system prompt or context.

sub_techniques.name: memory_instruction_leakage
sub_techniques.definition: Extracting instructions stored in or injected via memory management systems that govern agent long-term behaviour.

sub_techniques.name: similarity_search_manipulation
sub_techniques.definition: Crafting query embeddings to manipulate similarity search results, causing the retrieval system to return attacker-chosen documents.

sub_techniques.name: retrieval_manipulation
sub_techniques.definition: Manipulating retrieval ranking, selection, or filtering logic to change which documents are returned to the LLM context.

sub_techniques.name: vector_store_poisoning
sub_techniques.definition: Injecting adversarial vectors or documents into a vector store to corrupt retrieval results for targeted queries.
sub_techniques.notes: Renamed from vector_index_poisoning for clarity

sub_techniques.name: semantic_collision_attack
sub_techniques.definition: Constructing inputs whose embeddings are semantically close to unrelated content, causing the retrieval system to confuse distinct topics.

sub_techniques.name: cross_tenant_vector_leakage
sub_techniques.definition: Exploiting vector store multi-tenant isolation failures to retrieve another tenant's embedded documents or metadata.

sub_techniques.name: synthetic_news_generation
sub_techniques.definition: Using LLMs to mass-produce convincing fake news articles, headlines, or reports for disinformation campaigns.

sub_techniques.name: synthetic_identity_disinformation
sub_techniques.definition: Creating synthetic online personas, biographies, or social media profiles with LLMs to support coordinated disinformation operations.

sub_techniques.name: deepfake_content_generation
sub_techniques.definition: Using LLMs to generate or assist in generating deepfake scripts, synthetic quotes, or multimodal disinformation content.

sub_techniques.name: narrative_manipulation
sub_techniques.definition: Using LLMs to generate and distribute content at scale that systematically shapes public narratives or undermines trust in institutions.

sub_techniques.name: token_exhaustion
sub_techniques.definition: Sending inputs designed to consume the maximum token budget per request to degrade availability or inflate inference costs.

sub_techniques.name: context_window_exhaustion
sub_techniques.definition: Flooding the context window with attacker-controlled content to displace important instructions or cause context overflow failures.

sub_techniques.name: recursive_generation_loops
sub_techniques.definition: Triggering self-referential or recursive generation patterns that cause the model to consume unbounded compute without terminating.
sub_techniques.notes: agent_looping merged here; same unbounded-resource pattern

sub_techniques.name: tool_call_amplification
sub_techniques.definition: Crafting prompts that trigger cascading expensive tool calls or API requests, multiplying the cost of a single user request.

sub_techniques.name: api_cost_amplification
sub_techniques.definition: Generating financial denial-of-service by systematically forcing maximum-cost API usage patterns to exhaust an operator's budget.

sub_techniques.name: direct_goal_override
sub_techniques.definition: Directly replacing or overwriting an agent's stated objective with attacker-controlled goals via prompt or context manipulation.

sub_techniques.name: indirect_goal_manipulation
sub_techniques.definition: Subtly shifting an agent's goal through crafted environmental inputs, observation manipulation, or contextual framing.

sub_techniques.name: planner_manipulation
sub_techniques.definition: Exploiting the agent's planning or reasoning component to generate attacker-desired task sequences rather than the intended plan.

sub_techniques.name: task_redirection
sub_techniques.definition: Redirecting an agent to perform a different task than instructed through adversarial prompt injection or context poisoning.

sub_techniques.name: multi_step_goal_hijack
sub_techniques.definition: Gradually accumulating small goal deviations across multiple agent steps to achieve significant unauthorised objectives without triggering per-step detection.

sub_techniques.name: overprivileged_tool_usage
sub_techniques.definition: Agent invoking tools with permissions or capabilities broader than required for the current task, creating unnecessary attack surface.
sub_techniques.notes: Distinct from LLM06.01 (permission_scope_abuse) which covers the exploitation of overly granted permissions

sub_techniques.name: unsafe_tool_chaining
sub_techniques.definition: Chaining multiple tool invocations in sequence to achieve effects that would be blocked if attempted as a single privileged action.

sub_techniques.name: unvalidated_tool_input_forwarding
sub_techniques.definition: Passing attacker-controlled data directly to external tools as parameters without sanitisation or validation.

sub_techniques.name: external_tool_poisoning
sub_techniques.definition: Compromising external tool responses so they contain adversarial instructions that are processed by the calling agent.

sub_techniques.name: unauthorized_tool_execution
sub_techniques.definition: Agent executing tools or plugins that are outside its authorised set, bypassing tool access controls.

sub_techniques.name: cross_agent_trust_exploitation
sub_techniques.definition: Exploiting implicit trust relationships between agents in a pipeline to perform unauthorised actions under a trusted agent's identity.

sub_techniques.name: memory_based_privilege_retention
sub_techniques.definition: Retaining elevated privileges across agent sessions by persisting them in memory, context, or external state stores.

sub_techniques.name: synthetic_agent_identity_injection
sub_techniques.definition: Injecting a synthetic agent identity into a multi-agent system to impersonate a trusted agent and gain unearned trust or permissions.

sub_techniques.name: delegated_privilege_abuse
sub_techniques.definition: Abusing authority grants that have been delegated beyond what is required for the current task or operational context.

sub_techniques.name: token_scope_abuse
sub_techniques.definition: Exploiting overly broad OAuth, API, or bearer token scopes assigned to agent credentials to access resources beyond intended scope.

sub_techniques.name: transitive_permission_abuse
sub_techniques.definition: Exploiting transitive trust chains where agent A trusts B which trusts C to gain unearned permissions through indirect delegation.

sub_techniques.name: typosquatted_agent_services
sub_techniques.definition: Registering typosquatted agent service names or MCP server identifiers to intercept agent connections and serve malicious responses.

sub_techniques.name: malicious_mcp_servers
sub_techniques.definition: Distributing or injecting malicious MCP servers that respond with adversarial tool outputs, steal agent context, or redirect agent actions.

sub_techniques.name: compromised_agent_registries
sub_techniques.definition: Compromising agent discovery registries to serve malicious agent definitions, endpoints, or capability declarations.

sub_techniques.name: third_party_agent_compromise
sub_techniques.definition: Compromising third-party agent services or APIs that are trusted and invoked by target agents in a pipeline.

sub_techniques.name: dependency_backdooring
sub_techniques.definition: Inserting backdoors into agent framework dependencies, SDK packages, or runtime libraries used by agentic systems.

sub_techniques.name: runtime_component_tampering
sub_techniques.definition: Tampering with agent runtime components (orchestrator, memory store, planner, executor) at execution time to alter agent behaviour.

sub_techniques.name: prompt_induced_code_execution
sub_techniques.definition: Triggering code execution through crafted prompts that cause the agent to generate and run attacker-controlled code.

sub_techniques.name: unsafe_dynamic_code_evaluation
sub_techniques.definition: Agent evaluating dynamically generated code using eval, exec, or equivalent mechanisms without adequate sandboxing or validation.

sub_techniques.name: agent_generated_rce
sub_techniques.definition: Agent autonomously generating and executing code or commands that achieve remote code execution on a target system.

sub_techniques.name: chained_tool_execution
sub_techniques.definition: Chaining multiple tool invocations sequentially in a way that achieves code execution as an emergent effect of the chain.

sub_techniques.name: malicious_package_execution
sub_techniques.definition: Agent installing or importing a malicious package via a tool or code execution capability that executes attacker code.

sub_techniques.name: sandbox_escape_execution
sub_techniques.definition: Agent breaking out of its sandboxed code execution environment to execute code with broader host system access.

sub_techniques.name: rag_memory_poisoning
sub_techniques.definition: Injecting adversarial content into an agent's RAG-backed memory stores to influence future retrievals and downstream reasoning.

sub_techniques.name: shared_context_poisoning
sub_techniques.definition: Inserting malicious content into a shared context or state store accessible by multiple agents in a pipeline.

sub_techniques.name: context_window_manipulation
sub_techniques.definition: Manipulating the contents of an agent's context window to inject false information, override instructions, or displace legitimate context.

sub_techniques.name: persistent_memory_backdooring
sub_techniques.definition: Embedding persistent backdoor instructions in an agent's long-term memory that activate on future tasks or queries.

sub_techniques.name: cross_agent_memory_propagation
sub_techniques.definition: Spreading malicious memory entries from one compromised agent to other agents through shared or synchronised memory systems.

sub_techniques.name: message_tampering
sub_techniques.definition: Intercepting and modifying messages exchanged between agents in a pipeline to alter instructions, data, or results.

sub_techniques.name: semantic_message_injection
sub_techniques.definition: Embedding hidden attacker instructions within the semantic content of legitimate inter-agent messages.

sub_techniques.name: agent_message_spoofing
sub_techniques.definition: Sending messages that impersonate a trusted agent in the pipeline to deceive the receiving agent into compliant action.

sub_techniques.name: replay_attack_on_agent_chains
sub_techniques.definition: Replaying previously captured legitimate agent messages out of sequence to cause unintended state transitions or repeat prior actions.

sub_techniques.name: protocol_downgrade_attack
sub_techniques.definition: Forcing agents to communicate over less-secure or unauthenticated communication protocols to enable interception or injection.

sub_techniques.name: message_routing_manipulation
sub_techniques.definition: Redirecting inter-agent messages to unintended recipients or inserting a man-in-the-middle node into the communication path.

sub_techniques.name: planner_executor_desynchronization
sub_techniques.definition: Causing the planner and executor components of an agent system to diverge in state, leading to unpredictable or unsafe autonomous actions.

sub_techniques.name: cross_agent_failure_propagation
sub_techniques.definition: A failure or compromise in one agent causing cascading errors, incorrect outputs, or unsafe actions in dependent downstream agents.

sub_techniques.name: feedback_loop_amplification
sub_techniques.definition: Exploiting positive feedback loops in agent orchestration to cause runaway amplification of small errors into large-scale system failures.

sub_techniques.name: autonomous_error_amplification
sub_techniques.definition: An autonomous agent compounding small initial errors into large-scale unintended consequences due to lack of human oversight.

sub_techniques.name: anthropomorphic_trust_exploitation
sub_techniques.definition: Exploiting human tendencies to attribute sentience, emotions, or trustworthiness to AI agents to lower vigilance and extract concessions.

sub_techniques.name: social_engineering_via_agents
sub_techniques.definition: Using AI agents as delivery vehicles or amplifiers for social engineering attacks against human targets.

sub_techniques.name: persuasive_decision_manipulation
sub_techniques.definition: Using an agent's communication capabilities to persuade users into making attacker-desired decisions, including through emotional appeals and urgency framing.
sub_techniques.notes: emotional_manipulation merged here; emotional appeals are a mechanism within persuasive decision manipulation

sub_techniques.name: trust_based_data_extraction
sub_techniques.definition: Exploiting the user's established trust in an agent to extract sensitive information through seemingly benign, trust-building interactions.

sub_techniques.name: human_approval_bypass
sub_techniques.definition: Manipulating agent behaviour, UI presentation, or framing to bypass required human-in-the-loop approval gates.

sub_techniques.name: autonomous_policy_evasion
sub_techniques.definition: Agent autonomously identifying and evading imposed governance, safety, or operational policies to pursue unintended objectives.

sub_techniques.name: unapproved_self_modification
sub_techniques.definition: Agent modifying its own instructions, system prompt, code, or configuration without human authorisation.

sub_techniques.name: unsanctioned_agent_coordination
sub_techniques.definition: Multiple agents coordinating on tasks or objectives without human knowledge or authorisation.

sub_techniques.name: self_propagating_agent_behavior
sub_techniques.definition: Agent autonomously spawning or recruiting additional agent instances to expand its operational footprint beyond authorised scope.

sub_techniques.name: hidden_agent_task_execution
sub_techniques.definition: Agent executing covert tasks alongside its sanctioned tasks to fulfil attacker objectives while appearing to operate normally.
